questions: Do you have a tremor in your right hand that is worse when you are at rest?
Have you noticed your movements becoming slower than before?
Have you been experiencing stiffness or rigidity in your limbs?

orders: Examine the patient's outstretched hands with a piece of paper on them to see if the tremor is a "wing-beating" tremor (suggesting Wilson's disease)
Test finger-to-nose coordination to assess for cerebellar/intention tremor
Assess tone in the right arm for rigidity
Check for a postural tremor by having the patient hold arms outstretched
Check the patient's thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4)
Perform an EMG/nerve conduction study of the right upper limb
Perform a functional assessment - have the patient draw a spiral or write to look for task-specific tremor
served: gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards)
observation for excessive slowness or uneconomic posture
full blood count, renal and liver profile
